title: A statistical explanation of visual space

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of radial distances from scanner to physical locations in natural scenes (maximum at ~3 m)
findings.consequent: perceived distance of objects (2-4 m, 'specific distance tendency')
findings.mechanism: In the absence of distance cues, likelihood function is flat; apparent distance accords with prior probability distribution of distances.
findings.quote: distribution has a maximum probability at about 3 m... consistent with probabilistic explanation of 'specific distance tendency'.

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of differences in physical distances between two locations with small angular separations (maximum near zero)
findings.consequent: neighboring objects perceived at about the same distance ('equidistance tendency')
findings.mechanism: In the absence of information about distance differences, likelihood function is flat; perceived difference biases towards prior distribution.
findings.quote: distribution... for small angular separations... has a maximum near zero, neighboring objects perceived at same distance.

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of differences in physical distances between two locations with larger angular separations (lower probability for small absolute differences, flatter distribution)
findings.consequent: tendency to see neighboring points at the same distance from observer
findings.mechanism: Lower probability for small absolute differences in distance leads to a decreased tendency for equidistance perception.
findings.quote: probability for small differences lower... tendency to see neighboring points at same distance... decrease.

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of physical distances at eye level (Fig. 3c, black line)
findings.consequent: perceived distance of nearby objects presented at eye level
findings.mechanism: The shape of the probability distribution at eye level, combined with a Gaussian likelihood function, predicts overestimation for near distances.
findings.quote: perceived distance... linear function... near distances being overestimated.

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of physical distances at eye level (Fig. 3c, black line)
findings.consequent: perceived distance of farther objects presented at eye level
findings.mechanism: The shape of the probability distribution at eye level, combined with a Gaussian likelihood function, predicts underestimation for far distances.
findings.quote: far distances underestimated; crossover from over- to underestimation at 5-6 m.

findings.antecedent: probability distribution of physical distances at different elevation angles (shifts toward nearer distances with increasing absolute elevation angle, more pronounced below eye level)
findings.consequent: perceived location of objects on the ground (appear closer and higher)
findings.mechanism: Statistical characteristics of distance as a function of elevation angle account for perceptual effects of objects on the ground.
findings.quote: apparent location... predicted by probability distributions... is increasingly higher and closer to observer.

findings.antecedent: local dip in the ground plane (probability distribution of horizontal distances shifts toward greater distances)
findings.consequent: perceived distance of objects on the ground
findings.mechanism: Local terrain variations globally influence statistical configuration of the ground, leading to corresponding perceptual consequences.
findings.quote: expected overestimation when terrain deviates negatively from flat ground plane is about 0.2-0.6 m.

findings.antecedent: local hump in the ground plane (probability distribution of horizontal distances shifts toward lesser distances)
findings.consequent: perceived distance of objects on the ground
findings.mechanism: Local terrain variations globally influence statistical configuration of the ground, leading to corresponding perceptual consequences.
findings.quote: perceived distance... with a local hump should be slightly but consistently underestimated (by 0.1-0.5 m).

stimuli.description: Range image database of 20 natural outdoor scenes (512x512 pixels each) acquired by a laser range scanner (LMS-Z210 3D Laser Scanner, Riegl USA Inc.) mounted at eye level (1.65 m above ground). Data covered 326° horizontally and 24° vertically.
